 Jamal Murray (shin) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Rockets. 
 It’s unclear when the injury happened, but fantasy managers should be on the lookout closer to Monday’s contest. Murray is averaging 24.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 6.1 assists on the season, and has not yet missed a game. 
 -  Shawn Robinson

 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Jamal Murray recorded 16 points (6-of-13 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Nuggets. 
 Murray had a relatively quiet day at the office, scoring seven of his 16 points in the fourth quarter to help seal the victory. Category-league managers will be pleased with the rebounds and assists, but it would have been nice to see Murray end his week with a more prolific scoring performance. The Nuggets play three games in Week 4. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray put up 14 points (4-of-11 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, a steal and two 3-pointers in win over Raptors on Wednesday. 
 Jamal Murray didn’t have the most efficient night but still filled up the stat sheet in the win. He really got going in the second half which helped the Nuggets take off in the third quarter. We know who Jamal Murray is, and there’s no need to complain too much. He’ll bounce back and his next opportunity to do so will be against the Pacers on Saturday. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray led the Nuggets with 35 points (10-of-19 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, one block and four three-pointers in a 118-110 loss to the Trail Blazers on Monday. 
 Murray has been on a tear since the season opener. He was held to just six points in that game but has averaged 31.6 points, 6.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 5.4 triples while shooting 52.1 percent from the floor and 52.9 percent from deep in their five games since. This was his third game with at least 35 points in that stretch, and while it wasn’t enough for them to win, he continues to be a fantasy star and will look to stay hot against the Raptors on Wednesday. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray put up a monster performance of 39 points (10-of-18 FGs, 12-of-15 FTs), eight rebounds, five assists, a steal, a block, seven 3-pointers, and five turnovers in win over the Suns. 
 Jamal Murray was an absolute monster in the third quarter, getting 15 points and was the reason they got secure lead. He got to the line 15 times and hit them at 80% which should be a nice boost to your FT% category. He’s been what you hoped for if you drafted him in the top 20 this season. He won’t shoot this efficiently every night, but barring injury he’ll continue to do what he’s doing. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray finished Wednesday’s win over the Pelicans with 23 points (9-of-19 FGs), one rebound, six assists, two blocks and five three-pointers. 
 Murray has been consistently good on offense since scoring six points on 2-of-11 shooting in Denver’s season-opening loss to the Thunder. In Denver’s last three games, the Nuggets guard has shot 50.9 percent from the field while averaging 28 points per game. While the 42-point masterclass against the Pelicans has boosted the scoring average, Murray’s efficiency has been excellent. The Nuggets finish Week 2 with a road game against the Suns on Friday night. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray notched 19 points (8-of-13 FGs), six rebounds, eight assists, three steals and three three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors. 
 After going off for 42 points in Saturday’s win over the Pelicans, Murray cooled off a bit on Monday. However, he still shot well; the final line reflected lower shot volume and his inability to get to the foul line. After attempting 13 free throws against New Orleans, Murray didn’t attempt any against the Warriors. Monday’s outcome aside, Murray’s gotten off to a good individual start this season. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray led the Nuggets with 42 points (12-of-25 FGs, 10-of-13 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and eight three-pointers in a 141-135 overtime win over the Pelicans on Saturday. 
 After being held to just six points in the season opener, Murray bounced back in a big way in this game. He led Denver in scoring and accounted for over half of their three-pointers. He wasn’t able to get any offense going in overtime, but it was his heroics at the end of the game that forced the extra frame. He’ll look to carry this offensive production into Monday’s matchup with the Warriors, and fantasy managers shouldn’t expect to see many more six-point outings from him. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray recorded six points (2-of-11 FGs, 2-of-4 Fts), 10 rebounds, three assists and one steal in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder. 
 Murray shot 2-of-9 from the field in the first half of Thursday’s season opener. Unfortunately for fantasy managers who likely believed that things couldn’t get worse in the second half, they did. Murray scored just one point after halftime and recorded more turnovers (four) than field-goal attempts (two). With the Nuggets playing just two games during Week 1, fantasy managers will hope to see Murray rebound on Saturday against the Pelicans. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray accounted for 14 points (6-of-8 FGs), four rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Clippers. 
 Murray and the other Nuggets starters were shut down at halftime of Wednesday’s game, their penultimate preseason contest. He looked sharp, shooting 75 percent from the field overall. No matter how much Murray plays in Friday’s finale against the Lakers, his fantasy outlook won’t change much. He’s worth a second-round pick in 12-team formats. 
 Jalen Duren 
 DET 
 Center 
 #0 
 Jalen Duren, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Johnson, Tyrese Maxey and Jamal Murray were named third-team All-NBA on Sunday. 
 All five third-team selections were named All-NBA for the first time in their respective careers on Sunday. Duren’s selection may be the most impactful, as he’ll hit restricted free agency next month. The All-NBA selection makes him eligible for a max deal worth up to $287 million over five years. However, given his struggles during the postseason and the Pistons’ need to also address Ausar Thompson’s future, Duren may not strike it that rich this summer. Especially with other teams unable to offer a deal on par with what the Pistons can.

 Jeremiah Fears recorded 25 points (10-of-14 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers.
 Fears continues to spread his wings as the Pelicans’ point guard, scoring at least 19 points in three straight games and in five of his last six appearances. What’s especially encouraging for those rostering the second-year guard is that the return of Dejounte Murray (6/3/3 in 28 minutes) has not led to a decrease in production. Fears’ current fantasy value sits just outside the top-100, but that will change if he continues to play as he has over the last week. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Trey Murphy accounted for 26 points (9-of-17 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers.
 After shooting 12-of-28 from the field in his prior three appearances, Murphy made over 50 percent of his shots on Sunday. Add in the rebounds, assists and three-pointers, and this was a good finish to Week 3 for the Pelicans forward. The 26 points matched Murphy’s season high, and he’ll look to build on this effort when the Pelicans begin a four-game Week 4 on Monday against the Warriors.

 Zion Williamson finished Sunday’s loss to the Clippers with 25 points (9-of-9 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), four rebounds and two assists.
 Williamson produced excellent percentages in his final game of the week, much to the delight of those rostering him in category leagues. Unfortunately, the production outside of the points and percentages was pretty lean in the Pelicans’ 139-123 defeat. That said, over three weeks, Williamson’s production has exceeded his ADP (69) by a safe distance. The hope is that he can avoid the extended absence that has been a common occurrence throughout his NBA career.
